response.sql: WITH groups AS (SELECT link_to_major AS major_id, COUNT(*) AS member_count FROM member GROUP BY link_to_major), totals AS (SELECT SUM(member_count) AS total_members, AVG(member_count) AS avg_per_group FROM groups) SELECT g.major_id, g.member_count, 1.0 * g.member_count / t.total_members AS share_of_total, g.member_count / t.avg_per_group AS ratio_to_avg_group FROM groups AS g CROSS JOIN totals AS t ORDER BY ratio_to_avg_group DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Members with no major have NULL link_to_major, and SQL GROUP BY places all NULLs in one group. Empty-string link_to_major values, if any exist, are treated as a separate group, not as 'no major'.
The average member count per group is taken over all groups, including the no-major group, as the request specifies. Each member is counted once, and major_id is not checked against the major table.

The database is SQLite, which the TEXT/INTEGER/REAL schema suggests. Integer division is avoided by using 1.0 for the share and by AVG returning a real value for the average. Results are unrounded, as requested.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat empty-string link_to_major values as members with no major, so they join the no-major group together with NULLs.
alternatives.sql: WITH groups AS (SELECT NULLIF(link_to_major, '') AS major_id, COUNT(*) AS member_count FROM member GROUP BY NULLIF(link_to_major, '')), totals AS (SELECT SUM(member_count) AS total_members, AVG(member_count) AS avg_per_group FROM groups) SELECT g.major_id, g.member_count, 1.0 * g.member_count / t.total_members AS share_of_total, g.member_count / t.avg_per_group AS ratio_to_avg_group FROM groups AS g CROSS JOIN totals AS t ORDER BY ratio_to_avg_group DESC LIMIT 10;
